summary: The bill amends the Geothermal Steam Act of 1970 to waive federal drilling permits and exempt qualifying geothermal exploration and production from NEPA, ESA section 7, and most NHPA reviews when conducted on non-federal surface land where the U.S. owns less than 50% of the subsurface geothermal estate, if the operator submits a state permit.

scores.thoughts: The bill addresses federal permitting requirements and environmental review exemptions for geothermal activities. It contains no provisions related to government budgets, appropriations, or expenditures.
The bill makes no changes to tax rates, deductions, credits, or revenue collection mechanisms.

The legislation has no connection to firearms regulation or Second Amendment issues.

The bill explicitly exempts certain geothermal exploration and production activities from NEPA review, the Endangered Species Act, and (in some cases) the National Historic Preservation Act. These exemptions reduce federal environmental regulatory requirements for geothermal development on qualifying lands, directly limiting environmental protections and oversight.
